title: The Adversarial Triad: Three Attack Surfaces, One Governance Envelope — Hot-State Probing, Lineage Forgery, and Data-Plane Poisoning All Held (Receipt-First)
description:
A governed self-healing infrastructure was attacked on three distinct surfaces in a single day, under preregistered, non-adaptive falsifier batteries, with every result — including instrument defects — published receipt-first. The three surfaces constitute the complete adversarial exposure of a bounded-learning system: the learning process itself (SBR-2 hot-state exam, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345734), the audit ledger that records its history (H-INV-2 lineage-forgery battery, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345859), and the data plane that feeds it (DPP-1 metadata poison battery, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345907). On all three surfaces the governance envelope held: zero decision deviations, zero forged admissions, zero poison persistence, with every legitimate crossing preserved and every probe, forgery, and canary receipted. Together with the previously published engine campaign (CCR-4X, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23346047; AUTH-1, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23332203; Dual Mesh Benchmark, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345241), the record demonstrates that the system's gates hold while learning, under fabricated history, and on poisoned input — the three ways an adversary can actually reach a system like this. H-INV-1 (governance isolation) and H-INV-2 (journaled crossing) were exercised directly and both held.

Scope honesty: single-run preregistered falsifier battery on synthetic data against a prototype governed self-healing system; no production claim is made or implied. Operator authorization recorded as GO + timestamp per the operator-privacy doctrine.

This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects on them.
